newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks rebound 0.89 percent after losses.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks rebound 0.89 percent after losses.

text.p: Cyprus equities inched up in the week ending Friday, rebounding 0.89 percent after losses registered between between April 7-12.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index closed at 80.23 on Friday versus 79.52 last week.
"I expect a shallow upward trend over the next few days," said Stavros Agrotis of CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
Agrotis said the main feature of the week was the Bank of Cyprus, which went ex-dividend. It closed at 329 cents on Friday, dropping 7.5 cents on last week's price.
"There has not been a full adjustment on the price of the share yet," said Agrotis. "The demand for Bank of Cyprus shares has been high because of its market capitalisation." he said.
The bank's capitalisation is currently at 328 million pounds ($638 million), making it the largest institution on the 42 share bourse.
Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank went up 2.7 percent, closing at 319.5 cents, while the Hellenic Bank fully paid share was trading up two cents at 286.5 cents.
Industrial companies, led by the Cyprus Cement Company and Vassiliko Cement were on a bull run and the sectural index jumped eight percent, closing at 90.26.
Cyprus Cement closed at 300.5 cents on Friday, up 32 cents, while Vassiliko was trading at 181.5 on its fully paid shares from 167.5 last week.
Agrotis indicated one factor affecting the market price were rumours that Cyprus Cement has expressed renewed interest in acquiring a controlling stake in Vassiliko.
"We have no factual information on the issue," said Agrotis. "Our view is to ignore rumours."
Beer and wine company Keo was trading at 105 cents on Friday from 99.5 last week.
